solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Children's writer had turned left

indicators.note: turned tells us to read the word had from right to left

explanation.surface: Someone reports that an author of children's books had turned to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses HAD to DAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl wrote Matilda, The BFG and other much-loved children's books.

clue.text: Deposit Times editor, laid up with cataract

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom, reversed

parts.note: a cataract is a large waterfall, falls

explanation.surface: The Times editor is laid up in bed with a cataract on the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper; it is part of the definition, and 'cataract' is a waterfall, not the eye disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewfall is the time in the evening when dew begins to settle, a time of deposit.

clue.text: Joint bewilderment from reporters, Customs now prescribing seizure of partners for extortion

definitions.text: Customs now prescribing seizure of partners for extortion

parts.note: the hock is the joint in an animal's hind leg

indicators.note: reporters speak, so we want a word that sounds like the next piece

parts.note: daze means bewilderment

explanation.surface: A long-winded news story about customs officers seizing partners to extort money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Customs' looks like the border officials; it means traditions. On the Hock days after Easter, men and women in turn tied up the other sex for ransom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hocktide festival saw women bind men, then men bind women, releasing them for a payment.

clue.text: See red fluff withdrawn from zip

parts.note: to fluff a line is to blunder, to goof

indicators.note: withdrawn, drawn back, says the little word for 'from' is written backwards

parts.note: of can mean from, as in 'a man of Kent'
zip is slang for nothing, none at all

explanation.surface: Instructions for picking lint out of a trouser zip, or perhaps a paint colour reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' reverses the little word for 'from'. 'See red' looks like part of the instructions but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is to lose one's temper, which in British slang is to go off on one, a sudden rant.

clue.text: Having acquired door key, maybe I'll turn to check what's following me

indicators.note: to check is to hold back, so the reversed word restrains the note inside it
turn says the word for I is written backwards

parts.note: the ego is the self, I; the 'll is a link
in tonic sol-fa, fa comes after mi or me

explanation.surface: Someone muses about turning round to see who is following them.
explanation.walkthrough: Tonic sol-fa runs doh, ray, me, fah, so the note after 'me' is FA. 'turn' gives OGE; FA goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given a door key traditionally marked turning 21, reaching adulthood.

clue.text: An incarnation of Browning, do I turn up without water?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the reversed words stand outside the formula
in a down clue turning up means reading the words from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
I, one's self
water is H2O, two hydrogens and an oxygen

explanation.surface: A puzzled diver wonders whether to surface without water.
explanation.walkthrough: Browning here is the poet, not browning food. 'turn up' reverses DO SELF to FLESOD; 'without' puts it outside HHO.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleshhood, a rare word found in Browning's verse, means the state of being in the flesh, as an incarnation.

clue.text: Fantastic Provence with its sensational routes

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful, so the letters are spun into another shape

explanation.surface: A travel writer praises Provence and its spectacular scenic routes.
explanation.definitionFit: The optic nerves carry signals from the eyes to the brain, pathways for sensation of sight.

clue.text: Due around noon in confession? One has to be

indicators.note: around means the word for due goes round the letter

parts.note: money due is owing

explanation.surface: A confession due around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in confession?' is a further hint: owning up is confessing. 'One has to be' is the main definition: whoever has something is owning it.
explanation.definitionFit: To own is to have, so anyone who has a thing is possessing it.

clue.text: Talked about Springboks' tries?

indicators.note: talked about means the word is spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: the Springboks are South Africa's rugby team, so their things are SA's, said as letters

explanation.surface: Commentators discuss the tries the South African rugby team scored.
explanation.walkthrough: A rugby 'try' is a score; here 'tries' means attempts.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is an attempt, from the French essayer, to try.

clue.text: Highland town fuel supplier

definitions.meaning: a town in Caithness in the far north of Scotland
the cord of a candle or lamp that draws up wax or oil to the flame

explanation.surface: A Scottish town that sells fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Wick is a Caithness town in the Scottish Highlands, and a wick feeds fuel to a flame.

clue.text: Sweethearts Jeremy and Tim maintaining a period of abstinence

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the brothers' surname keeps the other letters within it

parts.note: Jeremy Vine and Tim Vine are brothers, a BBC presenter and a comedian, so together the Vines
Lent is the forty days of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Two famous brothers keep a sweetheart each while giving something up for Lent.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Vine is a British broadcaster and Tim Vine a British comedian; 'maintaining' holds the rest inside their shared surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A valentine is the person you choose as your sweetheart on 14 February.

clue.text: Dele, face to goal, blocks a last-minute opening for City

indicators.note: blocks means the two letters stand in the way, set inside the other piece

parts.note: something last-minute is late
dele, the proofreader's mark for deleting, is abbreviated D

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, so we take its first letter

explanation.surface: Footballer Dele Alli, facing goal, blocks a shot at the last moment for City.
explanation.walkthrough: Dele Alli was an England footballer, so 'Dele' sounds like a player; it is the proofreader's delete mark. D and G go inside A LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldgate was one of the gates in the old wall around the City of London, an opening into it.

clue.text: In an empty achievement lower classes at least get the point

indicators.note: in placed at the front says the following letters go inside the phrase

parts.note: void means empty
a feat is an achievement
D and E are the lowest UK social grades

explanation.surface: Even an empty triumph lets the lower orders understand the message.
explanation.walkthrough: UK market research ranks social grades A, B, C1, C2, D and E, so the lower classes are D and E.
explanation.definitionFit: In a league a draw earns one point, so not losing means at least picking up the point.

clue.text: Illegally obtain access to Marshal's horse

parts.note: to hack a computer is to break into it without permission
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: Someone breaks into the stable of a marshal's horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshal's' looks like the lawman owning the horse; it is Marshal Ney, and the 's is just 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackney is an ordinary riding horse, also a breed of high-stepping carriage horse.

clue.text: London District/Overground Line taking lots away from SW?

parts.note: a ley line is a supposed straight alignment across the land's surface
tons means lots, as in 'tons of money'
moving away from south-west is heading to the north-east, written TO NE

explanation.surface: A London Underground puzzle: which District or Overground line runs away from the south-west?
explanation.walkthrough: District and Overground look like Tube lines; 'District' belongs to the definition and 'Overground Line' is a ley.
explanation.definitionFit: Leytonstone is a district of north-east London, in the borough of Waltham Forest.

clue.text: Literary town, Ards, upset with necessary correction?

indicators.note: with tells us the correction is applied to the reversed word as well as being written out
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is reversed

parts.note: the fix needed is to put T in place of D, written T FOR D

explanation.surface: A literary town and the Northern Irish Ards peninsula are mixed up and need correcting.
explanation.walkthrough: Ards, upset, gives SDRA; replacing its D with T gives STRA, and the correction itself, T FOR D, is added on.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratford-upon-Avon is Shakespeare's birthplace, the most literary town in England.

clue.text: Each pole is new, but inferior

indicators.note: is new says the letters are made into a fresh word

explanation.surface: Each pole has been replaced, but the replacements are poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cheap and nasty, of low quality, is called el cheapo in jokey mock Spanish.

clue.text: Correspondence with which my Mrs has yet to get involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: Letters that my wife has not yet become involved with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correspondence' suggests letters; here it means matching parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Symmetry is exact correspondence of parts on either side of a line.

clue.text: Beneath the exterior of Tory hardliner there's a socialist, fiendish recklessness

indicators.note: below the outside of the word means the other letters sit inside it

parts.note: in British politics a dry is a hardline Thatcherite Conservative
red is the stock term for a socialist
fiendish means evil

explanation.surface: Under a hardline Tory exterior lurks a socialist with a fiendish reckless streak.
explanation.definitionFit: Daredevilry is wild bravery, taking dangerous risks for the thrill of it.

clue.text: Faulty principles adopted by FBI man

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in, so the principles go inside

parts.note: a fed is US slang for an FBI agent
law here means a body of principles or rules

explanation.surface: An FBI agent adopts faulty principles.
explanation.definitionFit: Flawed means having a defect, imperfect.

clue.text: Square's limited overs game

indicators.note: limited means bounded, so the first word encloses the letter

parts.note: to be square is to be even, quits
O is the cricket abbreviation for overs

explanation.surface: A cricket fan's limited-overs game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited overs' reads as one cricket phrase, but 'limited' is the indicator and 'overs' gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: Quoits is a game of throwing rings over a peg.

clue.text: Ill-disposed to duels as the last one laughing laughs?

definitions.text: as the last one laughing laughs

indicators.note: badly arranged, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to fight duels nonetheless laughs at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on the proverb 'he who laughs last laughs longest', here twisted to the loudest.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says whoever laughs last laughs best; here the final laugher's laugh is the most noisy.

clue.text: England 1966 squad member's breathing problem finally shifted by Ecstasy

parts.note: E is the usual abbreviation for the drug Ecstasy

indicators.note: the end of the word is altered, its closing letters changing places

parts.note: asthma is a condition that makes breathing difficult

explanation.surface: A footballer's asthma was eventually cured by taking Ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally shifted' moves the M of the illness to the very end, swapping the last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eastham was in England's 1966 World Cup-winning squad, though he did not play in the finals.

clue.text: Follow nuts seen going round the bend

indicators.note: going round means the scrambled letters surround the bend
nuts means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: a U-bend is shaped like the letter U

explanation.surface: Follow the nuts that were seen rounding the corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' turns SEEN into ENSE, which goes around U.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after, as a result or in sequence.

clue.text: A wave of wild theories about husband going after women

indicators.note: the rest follows the letter for women, so that letter comes first
about means the shuffled letters go around the other one
wild means the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Wild theories circulate about a husband chasing women.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of THEORIES, from 'wild', wraps round H to make HITEHORSE, after W.
explanation.definitionFit: A white horse is a wave with a foaming white crest, the kind seen in a stiff breeze at sea.

clue.text: Ace brings about unlikely set point

indicators.note: the ace is brought into the middle, with the other letters about it
unlikely means not as expected, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: In tennis, an ace wins an improbable set point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set point' reads as one tennis phrase, but 'set' is the anagram fodder (EST, from 'unlikely') and 'point' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four cardinal points of the compass.

clue.text: Office equipment in ideal home: rule comes out for new ID kit

indicators.note: for means in exchange, so the rearranged letters fill the gap left behind
comes out says the letter for rule leaves the estate agents' phrase

parts.note: des res, short for desirable residence, is estate-agent slang for an ideal home

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A home-improvement show: in the ideal home, the rule changes to allow a new ID kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns ID KIT into KTIDI, which replaces the R of DESRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Desk tidies are trays and pots that hold pens and papers on an office desk.

clue.text: Fish supply lines

parts.note: to do can mean to provide, as in 'we do lunches'
RY is the abbreviation for railway, the lines

explanation.surface: A fishmonger supplies lines for catching fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The John Dory is a flat sea fish, often just called a dory.
